newsitem.title: INDIA: India president agrees to help move budget.
newsitem.headline: India president agrees to help move budget.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma told parliament speaker P.A. Sangma on Saturday he would help parliament consider the budget for 1997/98 (April-March), Sangma's spokesman said.

"The president fully appreciated the situation (arising out of political uncertainties) and indicated that he would facilitate consideration of the budget by the house as the circumstances may warrant," the spokesman told Reuters.
"The speaker today called on the president and informed him about the decision of all parties for a budget session from April 21 to 23 for passing of the budget," the spokesman said.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Friday that parliament had agreed to pass the Finance Bill on April 21 to authorise government spending proposals.
Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition government, which lost the Congress party's make-or-break support on March 30, was on Friday defeated in a parliamentary confidence vote.

Lawmakers and Sangma had earlier expressed concern that state spending could be stopped if a Finance Bill and the vote-on-account authorising spending were not approved as a result of political uncertainties in parliament.

A pending Finance Bill presented by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on February 28 and yet to clear parliament contains tax-cutting budget proposals for 1997/98. The government has so far been authorised to continue spending under 1996/97 programmes through May.
